title: Levantine basics
variety: Levantine Arabic (Damascus and Beirut; a few common Palestinian and Jordanian words are marked)
about: The most common words of spoken Levantine Arabic that are not Standard Arabic: counted in 2.1 million words of Syrian, Lebanese, Palestinian and Jordanian text, most common first, 50 to a unit. It builds on the Arabic basics course: words you already know from Standard Arabic, even said a little differently (كْتير for كَثير), are left out, and the grammar course teaches the patterns. Every meaning is backed by a published dictionary entry. Each word has one short everyday sentence, with Levantine vowel marks and its English translation; ⟦ ⟧ marks the part that translates the word. A note under a word says how it differs from a Standard Arabic word that looks the same.
